The movie can make your head hurt. But not because it’s too convoluted to follow. It’s because the real convolution is: Why are we supposed to care? About any of this?
For all its flaws, in fact, GxK is second only to the underappreciated Godzilla: King of the Monsters among the Warner/Legendary reboot of these venerable characters.
Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire serves up a berserk dreamscape with plenty of payoff to please the MonsterVerse faithful. Shame about the human stuff, though.

“Let them fight!”, a human bystander once said in regards to Godzilla and some skyscraper-sized enemy. In terms of future endeavors regarding these two beloved legacy characters, we beg of you, MonsterVerse curators: Just let them be.
At one point in the film, Godzilla, weary from all that stomping around, lies down to take a well-deserved nap in the middle of Rome’s Colosseum. It’s the most relatable moment in the film.
They aren’t reinventing the wheel here, but fans ought to like it.
Despite a sluggish set-up, Godzilla x Kong does what it says on the tin. A neon rumble in the jungle that’s fun while it lasts, but easy to forget when it’s over.
It’s an achievement in absurd spectacle, a comically silly way to spend $135 million. I hope Warner Bros. keeps burning money this way.

A light, breezy, fun popcorn movie with plenty of kaiju fights! Kong and his storyline are particularly well realized, while the human cast has been very smartly slimmed down. Very accessible for casual fans, yet full of easter eggs for hard core fans.
Godzilla x Kong is kaiju comfort food. Wingard clearly loves this franchise and its monsters; that enjoyment is infectious.

Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire fully leans into the silliness but becomes a surprisingly dry affair whenever the two titular titans aren’t on screen.

It's no easy feat to make a boring film with these two iconic movie Monsters, yet GxKTNE bounds into the arena like a drunken kaiju and falls flat on its face without making any of the impact it, and its makers, are capable of.
It’s giant monsters fighting, the thing constantly shrugs: what else do you want? Ideally a bit more than this.
Instead of the title's rather inexplicable use of the multiplication sign, they shoulda called it GODZILLA PLUS/MINUS ONE, reflecting the fact that it’s both too much and not enough.

“Godzilla X Kong” makes up for its own deficiencies with oddball flourishes. Wingard and the writers work like rogue chefs at an Olive Garden, tossing everything they can at any number of walls to see what sticks.
Godzilla x Kong absorbs its disparate influences with glee, spitting out an adventure that hums with stimulating sound design, stuns with psychedelic visuals, and coasts on Titan-level charm.
More than previous chapters in the MonsterVerse series, Godzilla x Kong plays out as an elaborate but empty pantomime, anxious to avoid any form of subtext that might be deemed controversial.
There was real potential for this movie to be a strange action-packed odyssey. That potential was undercut, sadly, by a weak script and too many too conventional choices.
This new empire is a degradation of the one in our not-too-distant past.

Better and bolder than its predecessor, Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire delivers what viewers can expect to see when two titan monsters team up against a common enemy. There are less human characters who are irritating and more spectacular action.
“Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire” has very little road left to cruise, and it shows.
If you’re simply looking for a film that features oversized creatures punching each other in the face for 115 minutes, Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire is going to give you everything you want.

If this franchise is going to keep trying to get bigger, badder, and more smashmouth with the monsters, it's either going to need to level up the quiet moments amid the bombast or find a way to reduce them entirely.
While it doesn't compare to Godzilla Minus One, this is still a lot of fun, with a terrific, scene-stealing performance for Dan Stevens.

"Godzilla x Kong" is infectiously fun, raucous, and, in the 8-year-old sense, awesome. One will not take much away from "Godzilla x Kong," but you'll leave the theater with a big damn fool grin on your face.
When Godzilla x’es Kong — whatever the hell that means — everybody wins.
Godzilla x Kong is nowhere near a perfect movie & it suffers from plot contrivances, but it’s also thrilling & genuinely fun despite its shortcomings.
